newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore non-oil exports slump 6.3 pct in August.
newsitem.headline: Singapore non-oil exports slump 6.3 pct in August.

text.p: Singapore's non-oil exports fell a surprising 6.3 percent in August in nomimal terms year-on-year after rising 6.3 percent in July, the Trade Development Board (TDB) said on Friday.
Total non-oil exports were valued at Singapore $7.01 billion, the TDB said in its monthly trade report.
A Reuter poll of eight Singapore-based economists earlier in the week had predicted an average nominal year-on-year fall of 0.8 percent in August.
The actual August figure was lower than the lowest forecast in the Reuters poll, which ranged from a rise of 3.5 percent to a fall of 4.5 percent year-on-year.
In real terms, non-oil exports fell 2.8 percent in August to S$8.94 billion after rising 10.4 percent in July.

The TDB blamed the fall in exports on the slowdown in global demand for electronics and related products, which together account for almost half Singapore's total industrial output and around 60 percent of its non-oil exports.
"The slowdown was reflected in our key markets, mainly U.S., EU (European Union), Malaysia, Japan and Hong Kong," the TDB report said.
Economists admitted the August export figure was below their worst expectations.
"It is slightly below our expectations," said Liew Yin Sze, economist at brokerage J.M. Sassoon in Singapore. "We were going for practically no growth."
But he said there were signs that demand for personal computers was now picking up, which could mean better news for electronics exports in the future.

"I think we are probably close to the bottom of the cycle now, even though any kind of meaningful recovery will probably not be seen until the second quarter of next year in terms of a rise in Singapore exports."
